title: Context Prioritizer — scratchpad and rough PRD
content:
TL;DR: quick idea sketch for a product feature Im calling "Context Prioritizer" — heuristics + policy layer that decides which parts of conversation history (message chunks, embeddings, pinned facts) should be kept live in KV/prefix cache, which should be evicted, and which should be offloaded to cheaper storage (cold cache) for on-demand pull. Goal: reduce per-request token load and inference cost while preserving UX for long-running conversations and multi-turn apps.

Problem statement / motivation:
- Customers building long conversations or stateful assistants pay linear token costs to re-send large contexts or suffer latency for pulling long history from cold store.
- Current options: full session cache (expensive memory/GPU), naive eviction policies (LRU) that aren't semantic-aware, or manual developer work to surface important facts.
- We can add a small policy/learning layer that: 1) tags chunks with importance signals, 2) ranks for retention under budget, and 3) provides a simple API for app teams to pin or hint important spans.

Primary user scenarios:
1) Customer support assistant with 80+ turn session. Most turns are small; a few golden facts (customer profile, problem statement, previous workaround steps) are critical. Keep those on hot cache; evict the rest.
2) Multi-document agent that pulls from many sources over time. Keep embedding anchors and the top-k relevant docs in hot cache; re-embed/offload the rest.
3) Conversational CRM: sales rep pins a note mid-call ("decision: interested in enterprise tier") — that goes to high-priority bucket and is immune to eviction for N days.

High-level product proposal:
- New subsystem in session manager: Context Prioritizer service (lightweight, policy-first).
- Inputs: session events (messages, tool calls, embeddings, developer pin/hints, user reactions), model signals (attention salience, model-provided importance tokens), telemetry (turn frequency, latency budgets), developer config (hot_cache_budget bytes, retention_policy).
- Outputs: retention decisions (keep/hot, keep-cold, evict), TTLs, and a small metadata stream for observability (why-kept, score).
- API: optional SDK helpers for client-side pin/hint; REST route to set priorities; per-session view in Console.

User stories (rough):
- As an app developer, I can mark a message or slot as "pinned" so it stays in hot cache for N minutes/days.
- As an app developer, I can set a per-session hot-cache budget (tokens or bytes) and a retention strategy (semantic-prioritization | recency | manual).
- As an SRE, I can see prioritizer decisions on a per-session timeline to debug why a token was evicted.
- As a product manager, I can run an experiment toggling Context Prioritizer on/off for a cohort to measure token savings and latency changes.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Prioritizer can run in-host per-session with <2ms decision latency for typical events.
- Supports three priority buckets: HOT (KV on GPU/fast RAM), COLD (persisted & prefetchable), EVICT.
- SDK method: session.pin(span_id, ttl_seconds) -> confirmed pinned.
- Console: simple timeline view showing pins, evictions, and scores for sample sessions.
- Experiment: measure median tokens-per-session reduction >=20% on pilot workload without >5% drop in downstream task accuracy (measured by existing eval prompts).

Design notes / heuristics to explore:
- Heuristic features: recency, explicit user pin, model salience (model returns per-turn "importance score" via metadata), embedding similarity to pinned anchors, response length, tool usage frequency, user-specified slot importance tags.
- Scoring function: weighted linear model to start (w_recency, w_pin, w_model_salience, w_similarity). Keep weights configurable per-tenant.
- Cold cache: compressed embeddings + pointers to document store; prefetch when session activity predicts re-use (simple Markov model or thresholded score).
- Eviction strategy: within budget, sort by score ascending and evict until under budget; tie-breaker = oldest.

Telemetry & evaluation:
- Metrics to report: tokens_sent_to_model_per_session, hot_cache_hit_rate, cold_fetch_latency, accuracy_on_eval_set (per-feature), cost_delta_per_1k_sessions, false-eviction-rate (cases where user complains about missing context).
- Logging: store "why-kept" tags (pin/model_score/recency) to help debugging and to train future ranker.

Experiment plan (alpha -> beta -> GA):
- Alpha: internal-only, power users on hosted API with opt-in header X-Rd-Context-Prioritizer: alpha. Run on 10 customers. Manual pins only + model-sent salience. 2 weeks.
- Beta: add SDK pin API and tenant-configurable budgets. Expose console timeline. Run A/B test on 50 tenants. 4 weeks.
- GA: automated ranking enabled, per-tenant tunables surfaced, SLA docs updated.

Risks & unknowns:
- Model salience signal quality: we need an embedding/attention-based probe or ask model to return per-span salience reliably. Might need to iterate with research (Azra / Eleanor?).
- Privacy: pinned spans could contain PII — need to ensure KMS/HSM retention policies map. Coordinate with security + compliance.
- Complexity in observability: many quick evictions could be noisy; need good UX in Console to fold decisions and show representative examples.

Implementation sketch (runtime):
- Hook into existing session-manager event stream (serving-runtime). On message ingest, compute lightweight features and run prioritizer policy.
- If decision=HOT -> write to KV cache (current prefix cache mechanism). If COLD -> store in cold store (s3-like) with compressed index. If EVICT -> drop and emit event.
- Provide prefetch hook: when model request arrives, check population of hot cache; if missing but cold exists and predicted score>threshold, prefetch asynchronously before tokenization stage.
- Consider GPU memory pressure signals from infra to adapt hot_cache_budget globally per-pool.

Open todos / next steps (my immediate checklist):
- [ ] Quick spike to get model salience signal proof-of-concept (ask a gpt-like model to annotate message spans for importance). Tag: INF-3421.
- [ ] Pair with Maia in infra to see how to store "metadata.reason=why-kept" efficiently in current KV schema.
- [ ] Draft small SDK surface for session.pin(session_id, span_id, ttl).
- [ ] Get legal + security review on retention semantics (esp. pinned PII).

Notes to self / ideas to try later:
- Try a learned ranker after we collect labeled positive retention examples (train on why-kept logs).
- Auto-pinning heuristics for assistant-generated summaries: if model outputs "important facts" summary, auto-pin top-3.
- UI: one-click pin from Console + Slack integration to pin via slash command.

Slack refs / tickets I keep thinking about:
- #serving-runtime thread: "context-cache-ideas" (see messages 2024-12-03 onwards)
- Related tickets: JIRA-INF-3398 (session-ttl-tuning), JIRA-INF-3012 (kv-prefetch), GH-812 (prefetch infra PR)

Random brainstorm bullets:
- Could expose "importance budget" as developer-visible primitive (like tokens but lower-level).
- Offer a product tier where we promise N "pinned facts" retained across sessions (enterprise feature).

Conclusion: I like this as an incremental product that maps directly to cost/opportunity. It's a mix of lightweight product surface (pinning + budget) and a backend policy that can get smarter later. Next: quick spike on salience + talk to infra about integrated events.
